# Mahāsudassanajātaka (Ja 95)

**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Mahāsudassanajātaka* (Ja 95) is a story in the Pali Jātaka collection recounting a past life of the Bodhisatta as the righteous universal wheel-turning king (*cakkavatti*) Mahāsudassana [Appleton 2010; Jory 2016]. According to its framing narrative, the Buddha related this story on his deathbed in response to Ānanda's lament that the Master should not choose to pass into final Nibbāna in a small, remote town like Kusinārā [SuttaCentral]. The narrative describes the ancient grandeur of Kusinārā when it was known as Kusāvatī; King Mahāsudassana lived in magnificence, possessed the seven treasures of a universal monarch, and eventually retired to his Dhamma palace to devote himself to meditative absorption [Walshe 1987]. Lying down on his right side in the lion posture (*sīhaseyya*), mindful and fully aware, he peacefully met his end [Revire 2016].
Scholars recognize this narrative as a discourse jātaka closely related to the *Mahāsudassana Sutta* (DN 17) and the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16) [SuttaCentral; Walshe 1987; Appleton 2010]. In the early Dīgha Nikāya account, the story of Mahāsudassana is introduced with the archaic narrative marker *bhūtapubbaṃ* ("formerly"), whereas standard Jātaka commentary tales are introduced with *atīte* ("in the past") [Appleton 2010]. Scholars have observed that while the discourse versions in the Nikāyas represent an early phase of the genre without standard Jātaka terminology, the *Mahāsudassanajātaka* was later adapted and incorporated into the canonical Jātaka collection [Anālayo, Genesis of the bodhisattva ideal; Appleton 2010; Goldstone 1978].
Beyond DN 16 and DN 17, SuttaCentral lists verse and passage parallels in SN 15.20, SN 6.15, SN 1.11, and Thag 20.1 [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse data from DharmaNexus identifies internal Pali reuse between Ja 95 and the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), as well as cross-language alignment with the Tibetan *Ārya-mahākaruṇāpuṇḍarīka-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* [DharmaNexus].

- Mentioned in (SuttaCentral): Tha-Ap 21 Sopākattheraapadāna; Tha-Ap 429 Ekadhammassavaniyattheraapadāna; Tha-Ap 341 Dhammasavaniyattheraapadāna

- [Anālayo, Genesis of the bodhisattva ideal] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Genesis of the Bodhisattva Ideal — Notes that former-life accounts like the Mahāsudassana tale exist both as discourses and in the Jātaka collection.
